anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the AP63203WU (U8) feedback pin 1 is drawn on a net labelled 'FB' that carries a 51.1 kΩ resistor R13 to GND, sitting next to the L1/C9 output node that is labelled +3V3.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the fixed-3.3 V AP63203WU has its FB pin tied directly to the +3V3 output and that 'no external feedback divider is needed', i.e. no resistor should sit on the FB node.

evidence.quote: FB(1) is tied directly to +3V3 ... so no external feedback divider is needed
U8 AP63203WU, right-hand pin '1 FB', with 'R13 51.1k' to GND on the power sheet

anomalies.impact: If the FB pin is not directly on +3V3, the fixed-output buck loses its output sense and the 3.3 V rail can rise well above 3.3 V, damaging the ESP32-C3-MINI-1, the MAX31855s and the WS2812B; at minimum it puts an unintended network on the feedback node.

anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the +12V rail wire at the fan headers J7 and J8 appears to reach pin 1 as well as pin 2 of each 4-pin connector, so both top pins of each header sit on +12V.
anomalies.expected: The specification puts only 'the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)' on +12V; pin 1 of each header is the fan ground return and must be on GND.

evidence.quote: the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)
J7/J8 Conn_01x04_Pin with the +12V wire feeding pins 1 and 2 (power sheet, right side)

anomalies.impact: The fans receive 12 V on both their supply and ground pins, so they have no return path and cannot spin; the tach outputs stay inactive and the firmware will raise fan-stall run faults.

parsed.summary: The drawing matches the specification in most places, but the AP63203WU feedback pin carries a 51.1 kΩ resistor (R13) to GND where the intended design ties FB directly to +3V3, and the fan headers appear to put +12V on pin 1 as well as pin 2, so at least one connectivity deviation from the specified design is present.
